title: Pascal's Triangle II
prompt: Given an integer `row_index`, return the `row_index`-th (0-indexed) row of Pascal's triangle. In Pascal's triangle, each number is the sum of the two numbers directly above it (with missing entries outside the triangle treated as 0).
hints: You could build every row from row 0 up to row_index, storing each full row, but you only ever need the row before the current one.
Start with row = [1], and repeatedly build the next row from the current one: new row length grows by one each time, with 1s on both ends.
You can even update a single row array in place if you iterate from the end back toward the front, so you don't overwrite a value you still need.

solution.approach: Build the triangle row by row, but only keep the current row instead of the whole triangle, since each row depends only on the one before it. Start with row = [1]. To build the next row from the current one, walk from the right end toward the left, updating row[j] = row[j] + row[j-1] (this in-place, right-to-left order works because row[j-1] hasn't been overwritten yet), then append the trailing 1. Repeat row_index times. This is a rolling 1D DP over Pascal's recurrence, needing only O(row_index) space instead of storing the full 2D triangle.
